The outcome of the inquiry will likely shape how the United States plans for and responds to pandemics for years to come.
author: Hacker News

title: Crypto executive missing for four years, successor now under scrutiny
content:
Poland and Estonia announced a bilateral partnership on Thursday aimed at harmonising their approaches to cryptocurrency regulation and fostering cross‑border digital‑asset services. The agreement, signed in Warsaw by the Polish Ministry of Finance and Estonia’s Ministry of Economic Affairs, establishes a joint working group to develop common standards for anti‑money‑laundering (AML) compliance, consumer protection, and licensing of crypto‑exchange platforms operating in both countries. Officials said the collaboration will also explore the creation of a shared sandbox environment where fintech firms can test blockchain‑based solutions under coordinated supervisory oversight.

The initiative comes as both nations seek to position themselves as competitive hubs for digital‑finance innovation within the European Union, while aligning with forthcoming EU directives on crypto‑assets. By pooling regulatory expertise and facilitating seamless market access, the partnership is expected to attract investment from domestic and international firms and reduce operational barriers for existing providers. The working group is slated to deliver its first set of recommendations by the end of 2027, with the possibility of expanding the framework to include additional EU members in the future.
author: Hacker News

title: Sinaloa governor Ruben Rocha Moya seeks leave amid US drug trafficking charges
content:
Sinaloa’s governor, Rubén Rocha Moya, has submitted a request for a second leave of absence just days after resuming his duties, as authorities continue to investigate him on drug‑trafficking allegations. The request, filed with the state’s legislative assembly on Thursday, cites personal health reasons, though officials note it coincides with a federal prosecutor’s indictment that accuses the former mayor of Tijuana of facilitating the movement of narcotics through the state’s ports and highways.

The indictment, unsealed earlier this month, alleges that Rocha Moya used his political influence to shield cartel operations and received financial benefits in exchange for protection. He had previously taken a temporary leave in March to address the same accusations, returning to office in early August after a brief judicial review. The new request has reignited calls from opposition legislators and civil‑society groups for a permanent suspension or impeachment, while legal experts say the case will likely proceed through the federal courts, potentially barring him from holding public office if convicted.
author: DW World

title: Sydney Marathon medals feature incorrect German stadium engraving
content:
Runners participating in the 2026 Sydney Marathon will be presented with a commemorative medal that bears an engraving of Germany’s iconic Olympiastadion in Berlin. The decision, announced by the event’s organizing committee in March, aims to celebrate the marathon’s growing international partnerships and to highlight the historic venue’s architectural legacy.

The medal, produced by a local Australian mint in collaboration with German design firm Studio Kraft, features a detailed relief of the Olympiastadion’s distinctive sweeping roof and the 1936 Olympic rings, alongside the Sydney Harbour Bridge motif on the reverse side. Organizers said the dual‑nation motif reflects the marathon’s inclusion of a “global circuit” segment, which will see elite athletes from Europe and Australia compete side by side. The 2026 race, scheduled for October 10, is expected to attract over 15,000 participants, and the new medal will be awarded to all finishers as a token of the event’s cross‑continental collaboration.
author: BBC World

title: NAACP President condemns Navy's reported plan to replace Doris Miller carrier name with Trump
content:
NAACP President Derrick Johnson publicly condemned the U.S. Navy on Friday after reports surfaced that the service was considering renaming the aircraft carrier USS Doris Miller, the Navy’s first vessel to honor a Black World War II hero. Johnson’s social‑media post described the alleged discussions as “a slap in the face” to African‑American service members and to the legacy of Seaman First Class Doris Miller, who earned the Navy Cross for his bravery during the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941. The carrier, slated for commissioning later this year, has been celebrated as a milestone in the Navy’s efforts to recognize the contributions of minorities.

According to multiple sources, Navy officials explored alternative names, including that of former President Donald Trump, before the story was reported. The Navy has not confirmed any formal proposal to rename the ship, stating that naming decisions are made through a rigorous review process involving senior leadership and congressional input. Johnson’s criticism underscores ongoing debates over how the military commemorates historical figures and the broader push for greater representation within the armed forces. The Navy has indicated it will continue to evaluate naming options in accordance with established protocols.
author: The Hill

title: Exploring the Visual Artistry of Blade Runner
content:
A new feature article titled “The Art and Beauty of Blade Runner” was published on the cultural commentary site Nappertime.com, offering an in‑depth examination of the visual and thematic design elements that have defined the 1982 science‑fiction film. The piece explores the movie’s pioneering use of neon‑lit cityscapes, practical set construction, and the integration of industrial aesthetics with futuristic motifs, highlighting contributions from production designer Lawrence G. Paull and cinematographer Jordan Cronenweth. It also references the film’s lasting impact on contemporary visual media, noting how its blend of dystopian atmosphere and meticulous world‑building continues to influence filmmakers, game designers, and visual artists.

The article quickly garnered attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where it was posted under the discussion thread https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49405331. Within the community, the submission received 11 points and generated three comments, indicating modest engagement from readers interested in both the film’s artistic legacy and its relevance to modern digital culture. The discussion centered on the article’s analysis of Blade Runner’s aesthetic choices, with participants sharing additional observations about the film’s soundtrack, narrative structure, and its role in shaping the cyberpunk genre. The piece and its ensuing dialogue underscore the continued scholarly and popular interest in the visual craftsmanship of Blade Runner nearly half a century after its release.
author: Hacker News

title: Solar telemedicine kiosks improve healthcare access in rural Chad
content:
Solar‑powered telemedicine hubs are now operating in several remote districts of Chad, providing residents with real‑time consultations from physicians located in urban centers. The initiative, launched earlier this year by a partnership of the Chadian Ministry of Health, the World Health Organization and local NGOs, installs solar panels and satellite internet links at community health posts that previously lacked reliable electricity or broadband connectivity.

Since the rollout began, the hubs have facilitated more than 8,000 virtual appointments, reducing travel distances of up to 250 kilometres for patients and enabling doctors to diagnose and prescribe treatment for common ailments, maternal health issues and chronic diseases. Health officials say the model improves service continuity during the rainy season, when roads become impassable, and offers a scalable solution for expanding medical access across the country’s sparsely populated regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canadian premiers and PM Carney condemn US tariffs
content:
Provincial premiers across Canada have aligned themselves with Prime Minister Mark Carney in a coordinated response to the United States’ recent imposition of tariffs on a range of Canadian imports. The tariffs, announced by the U.S. president earlier this week, target steel, aluminum, and several agricultural products, citing concerns over alleged subsidies and trade imbalances. In a joint statement released from Ottawa, Carney and the premiers condemned the measures as “unjustified and detrimental to North‑American supply chains,” urging Washington to withdraw the duties and engage in constructive dialogue.

The Canadian officials highlighted the potential economic repercussions, noting that the tariffs could increase costs for manufacturers, raise prices for consumers, and strain the long‑standing trade relationship between the two nations. They also warned that retaliatory actions could be considered if the United States does not reverse its decision promptly. The coalition of provincial leaders, representing a combined economic output of roughly 70 percent of the country’s GDP, signaled readiness to coordinate with the federal government on any further steps, while calling for a swift resolution through existing trade mechanisms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump seeks to block BBC subpoenas for family members in defamation case
content:
President Donald Trump is seeking to prevent the British broadcaster BBC from subpoenaing his family members as part of the channel’s defense in his $10 million defamation lawsuit.  In filings submitted to the U.S. court on Saturday, Trump’s legal team argued that the BBC’s attempts to compel testimony from his children—Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump—and son‑in‑law Jared Kushner were “cynical” and a …  

The lawsuit, which centers on claims that the BBC defamed the former president, has drawn intense scrutiny as the broadcaster seeks to gather evidence to counter the allegations.  Trump’s lawyers contend that the subpoenas infringe on privacy and are an overreach, while the BBC maintains that the information is essential to its case.  The court has yet to rule on the motion, leaving the status of the subpoenas and the
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Susan Collins urges White House to weigh impact of US‑Canada tariff dispute
content:
Sen. Susan Collins (R‑Maine) urged the Trump administration to weigh the potential harm a tariff war with Canada could inflict on American consumers and businesses, diverging from many of her Republican colleagues. The call came after the White House announced new duties on Canadian steel and aluminum products following a breakdown in trade talks on Saturday. Collins warned that such measures could trigger retaliatory actions and disrupt supply chains that the U.S. relies on.

The negotiations had stalled over disputes on Canadian steel production quotas and the U.S. demand for Canadian lumber. While some Republicans applauded the administration’s hard‑line stance, others, including Collins, argued that the tariffs would raise costs for U.S. manufacturers and consumers alike. The split reflected a broader debate within the party about balancing trade protectionism with the economic interests of constituents.

As the new tariffs take effect, lawmakers on both sides are monitoring the impact on trade flows and domestic industries. The administration has indicated it will continue to seek a resolution, but the immediate consequence is a rise in prices for imported goods and a potential escalation of trade tensions between the two neighboring economies.
author: The Hill

title: Author Sets Trap for Book Marketing Scammer
content:
**Book‑marketing trap exposes pitfalls of modern publishing tactics**

Author RWW Greene’s recent Substack post, “I set a trap for a book marketing,” details a common yet risky promotional strategy that many indie publishers and self‑authors employ to boost sales. Greene recounts how a seemingly effective funnel—offering a free sample chapter in exchange for an email address, followed by a high‑priced book launch—can backfire when readers feel misled. The article outlines the psychological triggers that lure readers into the trap, the legal and ethical implications of bait‑and‑switch tactics, and the long‑term damage to author credibility and trust.

The piece sparked a lively discussion on Hacker News, where the post received 13 up‑votes and 9 comments. Readers praised Greene’s candid analysis and cited similar experiences with aggressive marketing campaigns that prioritize short‑term revenue over reader satisfaction. Critics on the thread argued that while some tactics skirt the line of transparency, they can be justified if clearly disclosed; others warned that even subtle manipulation could erode the indie publishing ecosystem’s reputation.

Greene concludes that sustainable book marketing hinges on honest communication and genuine value. By setting clear expectations and avoiding deceptive funnels, authors can build lasting relationships with readers, ensuring both ethical integrity and long‑term commercial success.
author: Hacker News

title: Scrap (2006) discussion garners 326 points and 177 comments on Hacker News
content:
A status update for the “Moxie” service was posted on the public status page at xcancel.com/moxie/status/2091218652133732491, drawing significant attention from the tech community. The post, which received 326 up‑votes and 177 comments on Hacker News, details a recent interruption in service and outlines the steps the team is taking to resolve the issue. Users and developers have responded with a mix of concerns about downtime, questions about the root cause, and suggestions for mitigation.

Moxie, a startup that offers a cloud‑based platform for real‑time data analytics, announced that a critical component of its infrastructure experienced a failure, causing a temporary outage for all users. The status page notes that the engineering team has identified the problem, applied a fix, and is conducting additional testing before restoring full functionality. In the Hacker News discussion, participants highlighted the importance of clear communication during outages, shared experiences from similar incidents, and debated the potential impact on Moxie’s customer base and future roadmap.

The exchange underscores the growing expectation for rapid, transparent incident reporting in the software industry. By publicly documenting the outage and the corrective actions, Moxie aims to maintain trust with its users while working to prevent recurrence. The community’s engagement suggests that stakeholders are closely monitoring the resolution timeline and the company’s plans for strengthening its infrastructure.
author: Hacker News

title: Flipkart's quick‑commerce unit handles up to 1.2 million orders daily, closing in on rivals
content:
Flipkart’s quick‑commerce division has begun handling between 1.1 million and 1.2 million orders each day, a volume that is almost three times the level recorded in November. The surge reflects the rapid scaling of the platform’s ultra‑fast delivery service, which targets delivery within minutes to a few hours.

The increase follows a concerted expansion of the venture’s logistics network, including the addition of new fulfillment hubs and a larger fleet of delivery personnel across major Indian cities. By the end of the month, the daily order count rose from roughly 400,000 in November to the current range, indicating a sustained uptick in consumer demand for rapid‑delivery options. The growth aligns with broader trends in the Indian e‑commerce sector, where quick‑commerce models are gaining market share.

Analysts note that the heightened order flow positions Flipkart’s quick‑commerce arm as a significant player in the fast‑delivery segment, potentially influencing competitive dynamics and future investments in the space. The company is expected to continue expanding its infrastructure to support the higher volume and maintain service speed.
author: TechCrunch

title: Thousands flee Kordofan fighting, seek safety in El Obeid
content:
Thousands of residents have fled the escalating clashes in Sudan’s Kordofan region, seeking refuge in the provincial capital of El Obeid, where they hope to find relative safety. The displacement follows intensified fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces that began in early May, prompting residents of towns such as Al‑Ubayyid, El‑Obeid’s surrounding districts, and other conflict‑affected localities to abandon their homes. Humanitarian agencies estimate that the exodus has added several thousand people to the city’s already strained population, overwhelming local shelters and basic services.

Aid groups and local authorities report that the influx has heightened demand for food, water, and medical assistance, while security checkpoints around El Obeid remain active to monitor movements and prevent further violence from spilling into the city. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has called for increased funding to support emergency response efforts, emphasizing the need for safe corridors and additional shelter capacity. As fighting continues in Kordofan, officials warn that displacement numbers could rise, underscoring the importance of sustained humanitarian aid and protection measures for those seeking safety in El Obeid.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canada to impose tariffs on US steel, electronics starting September 8
content:
Canada announced that, beginning on September 8, it will levy tariffs on a range of imports from the United States, including steel, electronics and several other product categories. The policy was disclosed by Mark Carney, Canada’s senior economic official, who said the measures are intended to address perceived imbalances in the bilateral trade relationship and to protect domestic industries from what officials describe as unfair pricing practices.

The tariffs will apply to specific grades of steel and a selection of electronic goods, with rates to be set by the Canada‑U.S. Trade Commission after a review period. Government spokespeople indicated that the move follows a series of consultations with Canadian manufacturers and aligns with broader trade‑policy objectives aimed at safeguarding local production. The implementation date gives U.S. exporters a short window to adjust to the new regime, and both countries are expected to engage in further negotiations to resolve outstanding trade disputes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Mourinho's first match back at Real Madrid ends in 90th‑minute win over Espanyol
content:
José Mourinho returned to Real Madrid’s Bernabéu for his first match in charge after a 12‑year absence, guiding the club to a 1‑0 victory that came from a 90th‑minute strike. The win, achieved against Espanyol, marked the culmination of a day of celebrations, frustrations and a sense of relief for the former Portugal coach, who had been absent from the club for 4,380 days.

Mourinho’s approach to the game was measured. Rather than joining the bench in a flurry of celebration, he walked down the touchline, watched his players celebrate, and spoke privately with captain Fede Valverde. The match also highlighted his task of blending a new star‑studded lineup—Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham—while integrating the club’s most expensive signing to date, 21‑year‑old Yan Diomande, who came from Levante and scored the decisive goal.

The victory underscores Mourinho’s calm leadership and his ability to manage a high‑profile squad. With a win to start his tenure, the coach has demonstrated that he can harness the talents of his marquee players and the emerging talent of Diomande, setting a foundation for the challenges ahead in La Liga and European competition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arthur Fils defeats Flavio Cobolli to reach Cincinnati Masters final
content:
French teenager Arthur Fils captured the spotlight in the Cincinnati Open’s men’s semi‑finals by defeating the No. 7 seed, Italian Flavio Cobolli, in straight sets, 6‑3, 6‑4. The match began with a rain‑delayed, uneven rhythm that left Fils scrambling at the baseline, his serve stalled at 3‑3. Cobolli’s aggressive net play seemed poised to finish the point, but Fils responded with a powerful passing forehand that sent the ball over Cobolli’s head, earning a roar from the crowd and turning the tide in his favour.

From that pivotal point, Fils asserted control, combining athleticism, speed, and tactical precision to dominate the remainder of the contest. His relentless pressure and accurate groundstrokes dismantled Cobolli’s rhythm, allowing the Frenchman to secure his first Masters 1000 final appearance at the Cincinnati Open. The victory underscored Fils’ growing reputation as a rare, exciting talent capable of rising to the occasion against higher‑seeded opponents.

With the win, Fils will now face the women’s champion in the final round of the tournament, while the men’s field looks forward to a thrilling conclusion. The match showcased the unpredictable nature of Grand Slam‑level tennis, where a single moment of brilliance can shift momentum and alter the outcome of a hard‑fought contest.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia vs Bangladesh Day Two of Second Test Live Updates
content:
Updates from the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay show Australia on the brink of a high‑scoring chase, trailing by a single run after 44 overs. The score stands at 183‑8 with Green on 64 and Lyon on 15. In the 44th over, Shoriful resumed his spell, delivering a bouncer that struck Lyon’s thigh pad. Lyon appealed for LBW, but the umpire declined to consider a review, and the over ended with a maiden from Shoriful. The next over, the 45th, saw Taijul Islam entering the attack with his left‑arm orthodox spin. Green defended the first ball and then rotated the strike, giving Lyon a brief chance to face a fellow spinner, but only one run was taken.

The match has drawn attention beyond the on‑field action. A note to Megan indicates that the selection process is not being driven by run totals alone, citing Picky Ponting’s observation that in the last Shield season only three of the top twenty‑two run‑scorers averaged above 40—Renshaw, Carey, and Weatherald. This highlights a broader debate about the criteria used for team selection, suggesting that consistency and other factors may be weighted more heavily than sheer run accumulation.

With Australia now at 184‑8 after the 45th over, the contest remains tightly contested. The remaining overs will determine whether the Australian side can close the gap or secure a victory. As the game progresses, analysts and selectors alike will continue to monitor both the immediate performance on the field and the longer‑term implications for squad composition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Long-nosed fur seal dies from H5 bird flu in South Australia, first mainland mammal case
content:
A long‑nose fur seal was discovered dead on the sands of Beachport, South Australia, on Wednesday, marking the first confirmed case of the H5 subtype of avian influenza in a mammal on the Australian mainland. The death comes amid a growing wave of outbreaks that has already claimed more than 1,000 greater crested terns on offshore islands, as reported by Premier Peter Malinauskas. The seal’s demise is seen as a further indication that the virus is spreading beyond its initial avian hosts.

Federal agriculture minister Julie Collins described the seal’s death as “not unexpected” as the disease continues to move through the country. The incident follows the Premier’s announcement of three mass mortality events on islands along the Limestone Coast, underscoring the escalating reach of the virus across both marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Authorities are monitoring the situation closely and have increased surveillance of wildlife populations in the region.

The finding signals a significant shift in the epidemiology of H5 bird flu, raising concerns about potential wider impacts on wildlife and public health. Continued vigilance and rapid response measures will be essential to contain the outbreak and protect vulnerable species across Australia.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Figmimic bookmarklet copies webpages into Figma as editable layers
content:
A new design‑to‑code utility, Figmimic, has been released by developer Marcua. The lightweight tool pulls design data from Figma files and generates clean, reusable code snippets that can be dropped into a project. The project’s web page (marcua.net/minitools/figmimic/) outlines the workflow, showing how designers can export components and have the tool produce corresponding HTML, CSS, or React code with minimal manual tweaking.

Figmimic’s core features include automatic layout translation, support for responsive breakpoints, and the ability to map design tokens to CSS variables. The tool is intended for rapid prototyping and for teams that want to keep design and implementation tightly coupled without the overhead of larger design‑system frameworks. On Hacker News the post has garnered 19 points and no comments, indicating modest but focused interest from the community.

While the project is still in its early stages, Marcua plans to expand Figmimic’s language support and improve integration with version‑control workflows. The tool’s straightforward interface and open‑source nature make it a potential asset for designers and developers looking to streamline the hand‑off process and reduce the time between design approval and functional code.
author: Hacker News

title: Software Engineering in the Agentic Era article published Feb 23 2026
content:
Simon Willison’s latest blog post, “Agentic Engineering Patterns,” was published on February 23, 2026, and has already attracted attention from the tech community. The article explores a new framework for designing software systems that incorporate autonomous agents—software components that can make decisions, learn from data, and interact with users or other systems without constant human oversight. Willison argues that existing engineering practices are ill‑suited for such systems and proposes a set of patterns that address common pitfalls such as state management, safety, and interpretability.

In the post, Willison outlines several concrete patterns, including “Modular Decision Loops,” which separate perception, planning, and execution into distinct, testable units, and “Safe Exploration,” which limits an agent’s actions to a predefined safe set while still allowing it to learn. He also discusses the importance of clear interfaces between agents and their environment, recommending the use of standardized message protocols and rigorous logging to aid debugging and compliance. The article draws on examples from recent AI applications, such as autonomous customer‑service bots and adaptive recommendation engines, to illustrate how the patterns can be applied in practice and how they improve maintainability and transparency.

Willison concludes that adopting these agentic engineering patterns can help organizations build more reliable, auditable, and scalable autonomous systems. He encourages readers to experiment with the patterns in their own projects and to contribute feedback through the comments section of the blog. The post has already generated modest engagement, with three upvotes and no comments on the Hacker News discussion thread linked in the article.
author: Hacker News

title: Iran warns of retaliation against nations joining US economic sanctions
content:
Tehran has issued a stark warning that any nation aligning with the United States in its economic campaign against Iran will be met with “tit‑for‑tat” measures, the Iranian foreign ministry said on Wednesday. The statement came as the United States intensified sanctions targeting Iran’s oil exports, banking sector and key industries, accusing Tehran of supporting militant groups and pursuing a nuclear program that breaches international obligations.

Iran’s officials indicated that retaliatory actions could include reciprocal sanctions, restrictions on trade and the possible targeting of foreign assets linked to participating countries. The warning underscores the heightened diplomatic tension surrounding the U.S. “maximum pressure” strategy, which has already drawn criticism from several European and Asian states wary of the broader impact on global markets. Tehran’s message serves as a reminder that the dispute over Iran’s economic isolation is likely to expand beyond bilateral measures, potentially reshaping regional trade dynamics.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran warns neighboring states against joining US economic war
content:
Tehran’s foreign ministry spokesperson warned on Monday that any nation aligning itself with the United States would be deemed an adversary of Iran, and that the Iranian government would consider targeting that country’s interests in retaliation. The statement was issued in response to recent diplomatic moves by several Middle Eastern states that have sought closer security cooperation with Washington, including discussions about joint military exercises and intelligence sharing.

The official emphasized that Iran views such alignments as direct threats to its national security and warned that Tehran would take “necessary measures” to protect its strategic assets, citing potential actions against economic projects, diplomatic missions, and regional partners of the implicated state. The remarks come amid heightened tensions in the region, where both Tehran and Washington have been expanding their respective influence, and underscore the risk of further escalation should additional states formalize ties with the United States.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Swedish sword attack kills 17-year-old girl, injures two boys, suspect detained
content:
An attack earlier today left two boys, aged 12 and 17, injured, according to officials. Emergency services responded to the scene, providing medical assistance to the victims before transporting them to a nearby hospital for treatment.

Law enforcement officials confirmed that an 18‑year‑old suspect has been detained in connection with the incident. The authorities are continuing their investigation, and further details will be released as they become available.
author: BBC World

title: Syria says Israeli strike near Damascus breaches international law
content:
The latest incident, reported early Monday, involved an unidentified explosion near the Syrian‑Turkish frontier that prompted an immediate security response from both local authorities and neighboring states. Preliminary statements from the Syrian Ministry of Defense indicated that the blast occurred in a contested area close to the Turkish border, though casualty figures and the precise cause remain unconfirmed pending further investigation. Regional monitoring groups have begun compiling satellite imagery and eyewitness accounts to ascertain whether the event was the result of an airstrike, artillery fire, or another form of hostile activity.

The development follows reports from earlier this week that Israeli forces had struck a military airbase situated near the same border region, a target allegedly used by Iranian‑backed militias. Turkish officials have previously expressed concern over the proximity of such operations to their territory, urging restraint and calling for transparent communication to prevent escalation. As diplomatic channels remain active, the international community is watching closely for any further incidents that could destabilize an already volatile border area.
author: BBC World

title: Cottage Cheese Health Claims Lack Strong Evidence
content:
Cottage cheese has surged in popularity, finding its way into dips, batters, pizza crusts and even brownies. Food‑tech influencers and recipe blogs tout the dairy product as a high‑protein staple that can aid muscle building and fat loss, sparking a wave of viral “cottage‑cheese‑powered” dishes across social media.

Nutritionists note that cottage cheese does contain roughly 11–12 grams of protein per 100‑gram serving, along with calcium, potassium, and B‑vitamins. However, peer‑reviewed studies that directly link cottage‑cheese consumption to significant gains in lean muscle mass or accelerated weight loss are scarce. Most evidence supporting its benefits comes from broader research on high‑protein diets, not from isolated investigations of cottage cheese itself.

While the ingredient’s versatility and protein content make it an appealing addition to many meals, consumers should view the muscle‑building and fat‑loss claims with caution. As the trend continues, further research will be needed to substantiate the specific health benefits attributed to cottage cheese.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Iran warns neighboring states not to join US economic pressure campaign
content:
Washington has issued a formal warning that the United States is prepared to intensify economic measures aimed at Iran, a move that aligns with President Donald Trump’s recent statements pledging to further isolate the Iranian government. The warning, delivered by senior officials at the State Department, cautioned that any perceived escalation in Tehran’s regional activities could trigger additional sanctions targeting Iran’s banking, oil, and trade sectors, thereby tightening the financial constraints already imposed on the country.

President Trump’s approach reflects a broader strategy to weaken Iran’s government by curbing its revenue streams and limiting its access to international markets. The administration has highlighted concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and its support for proxy groups across the Middle East, arguing that heightened economic pressure is necessary to compel compliance with U.S. demands. Analysts note that the proposed measures could exacerbate Iran’s economic challenges, potentially influencing domestic stability and regional dynamics, while also prompting reactions from European allies and other stakeholders invested in diplomatic negotiations with Tehran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US-Canada Trade Dispute Escalates: 50% Tariff Imposed, Canada Retaliates
content:
Negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed over the weekend, prompting the Trump administration to impose a 50 percent tariff on Canadian goods. The move was intended to pressure Canada into revising trade terms that the U.S. deemed unfavorable. In response, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a retaliatory tariff on U.S. products, stating during a Saturday press conference that Canada would “match Washington’s” tariff.

The U.S. tariff targets a range of Canadian imports, including agricultural products and manufactured goods, and is part of a broader strategy to renegotiate trade agreements. Canada’s counter‑tariff is expected to affect similar categories of U.S. exports, potentially escalating the trade dispute. Both leaders indicated that the tariffs would remain in place until a new agreement is reached, and they urged their respective governments to resume negotiations promptly.

The swift reciprocal action underscores the heightened tensions in North American trade relations. While the tariffs may impose costs on consumers and businesses in both countries, the administrations have signaled a willingness to engage in further talks. The next phase will likely involve diplomatic efforts to resolve the impasse and restore the status quo of bilateral trade.
author: The Hill

title: Haida Gwaii Recovers First Marbled Murrelet Nest in 30 Years
content:
A small expedition team set out from the southern coast of Haida Gwaii on a late‑summer day, crossing the Dixon Entrance in an open skiff before trekking into the island’s interior. The group, composed of four hikers and a marine biologist, navigated the turbulent waters head‑on, battling swells and salt spray as they crossed the narrow channel that separates the archipelago from mainland British Columbia.

After the sea crossing, the team entered the dense salal understory and wove between towering western red cedars that line the northern part of the island. The forest, shrouded in twilight, presented a stark contrast to the open sea they had just left. The journey, which took several days, highlighted the logistical challenges of moving through remote wilderness while maintaining communication and safety protocols in an area with limited infrastructure.

The expedition underscores the rugged nature of Haida Gwaii’s landscape and the resilience required to traverse it. While the team successfully reached their destination, the experience serves as a reminder of the delicate balance between exploration and environmental stewardship in this pristine region.
author: Phys.org

title: Heatwaves threaten school calendar as teachers report classroom challenges
content:
Teachers across the country are warning that the increasing intensity of summer heat could make it progressively harder for classrooms to operate effectively during the hottest months. In statements gathered from several school districts, educators cited rising ambient temperatures, limited ventilation, and the absence of air‑conditioning in many older school buildings as primary concerns. The warnings come after a series of record‑breaking heatwaves that have pushed daily highs above 95°F (35°C) in many regions, prompting health officials to issue heat advisories for vulnerable populations, including children.

According to a recent survey conducted by a national teachers’ association, more than 70 percent of respondents reported that excessive heat had already disrupted lesson plans, reduced student concentration, and increased fatigue among both pupils and staff. Several districts have responded by adjusting school calendars, shortening recess, and installing temporary cooling units, but many schools lack the funding or infrastructure to implement comprehensive climate‑control solutions. Experts note that prolonged exposure to high indoor temperatures can impair cognitive performance and exacerbate health risks, potentially widening educational inequities in communities with older facilities.

Education officials acknowledge the teachers’ concerns and are reviewing strategies to mitigate heat‑related disruptions. Proposed measures include expanding the use of shaded outdoor learning spaces, upgrading HVAC systems, and revising school schedules to avoid the peak heat of the day. The ongoing dialogue underscores the need for coordinated action as climate trends suggest that extreme summer temperatures will become more frequent in the coming years.
author: BBC Science

content:

title: Tottenham Lose 3-0 to Brentford; De Zerbi Criticises Team
content:
Tottenham Hotspur opened the Premier League season with a 3‑0 defeat at Brentford, a result that has prompted the manager to question the squad’s readiness. The North London club, which narrowly avoided relegation last year and is expected to spend more than £300 million on new players, was unable to match the hosts at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Brentford dominated the match, exploiting gaps in Tottenham’s defence and demonstrating superior fitness and tactical execution. Manager Roberto De Zerbi criticised his side’s lack of physical conditioning and fight, citing the pre‑season tour of Australia as a contributing factor to the poor performance. The loss has highlighted the gap between Spurs and the league’s top teams, raising doubts about their ability to compete without significant reinforcement.

The defeat serves as a stark reminder for Tottenham of the challenges that lie ahead. With a heavy transfer budget earmarked for the summer, the club will need to address the physical and tactical deficiencies exposed in the opening game if it hopes to avoid another season of struggle.
author: Guardian Sport

content:
A new post has appeared on the “Thinking in Python” website, a popular resource for Python developers. title: Tropical Storm Moke approaches Hawaii's Big Island with heavy rain and strong winds
content:
Hawaii’s largest island, commonly called the Big Island, is confronting a renewed threat as an intensifying storm approaches for the second consecutive week. The National Weather Service has issued a tropical storm watch for the island’s eastern and southeastern coasts, indicating sustained winds of 39–73 mph and the possibility of heavy rainfall, strong gusts, and localized flooding. The system, which has been gaining strength over the warm Pacific waters, is projected to move northwestward toward the island by early Thursday, prompting officials to activate emergency response protocols.

State and county agencies have begun pre‑emptive measures, including positioning sandbags in vulnerable low‑lying areas, securing public facilities, and urging residents to review evacuation routes and emergency kits. The Department of Transportation has placed extra crews on standby to clear roadways and restore power should outages occur. Historically, the Big Island’s topography—marked by steep slopes and volcanic terrain—has amplified storm impacts, making the current advisories especially critical. Authorities will continue to monitor the storm’s development and issue updates as conditions evolve, aiming to mitigate potential damage and ensure public safety.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Office star Davis thanks supporters after cancer diagnosis
content:
The Office star appeared at the London Comic Con on Thursday, marking a public engagement less than two weeks after she disclosed a serious health condition. The surprise appearance took place at the ExCel Centre, where the actress participated in a panel discussion alongside fellow cast members and answered questions from a packed audience of fans and media representatives. Organizers confirmed that the star’s presence was confirmed only after her recent announcement, and she was greeted with a standing ovation upon taking the stage.

title: Real Madrid defeat Espanyol 2-1 in Mourinho's return match
content:
Real Madrid secured a 2‑1 victory after a dramatic finish in which substitute Carlos Espi netted the decisive goal in the closing minutes. Jude Bellingham opened the scoring early in the first half, giving the visitors an early lead, while Alex Calatrava restored parity for the home side shortly before halftime. The match, played at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday, saw both teams create multiple chances, but it was Espi’s late strike that ultimately tipped the balance in Madrid’s favor.

The win moves Real Madrid up the league table, extending their unbeaten run and reinforcing their position among the title contenders. Espi’s goal, coming in the 86th minute, underscored the squad’s depth and the impact of tactical substitutions. With three points added, the team will look to build on the performance in their upcoming fixtures, while Calatrava’s contribution highlighted the resilience of the opposition despite the defeat.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Harvard Bootcamp Uses AI Avatars to Coach Startups
content:
Harvard Business School’s Foundry program has introduced AI avatars to provide real‑time feedback during practice pitches and simulated board meetings. The avatars, powered by advanced natural‑language processing and behavioral analytics, evaluate presentation style, content clarity, and persuasive techniques, offering suggestions that mirror the insights a seasoned investor or board member might give. Participants can rehearse multiple iterations, receiving data‑driven critiques on tone, pacing, and strategic framing before facing actual investors.

The initiative is part of Foundry’s broader effort to blend technology with experiential learning. By integrating AI‑generated feedback, the program aims to accelerate skill acquisition and reduce the variability that comes from relying solely on human coaches. Early pilots have shown that students who use the avatars report higher confidence levels and a clearer understanding of how to tailor their messaging to diverse stakeholder audiences.

While the program remains in a testing phase, its success could signal a shift in executive education toward more scalable, tech‑enabled coaching models. If adopted widely, AI avatars may become a standard tool for entrepreneurs and executives seeking to refine their pitch and negotiation tactics in a controlled, data‑rich environment.
author: TechCrunch

title: Open-air cinema revives movie nights in Khartoum
content:
Families have begun gathering again at an open‑air cinema in Khartoum, marking a modest return to communal entertainment amid the city’s ongoing conflict. The temporary venue, set up in a fenced courtyard near the central district, screens popular Arabic and international films twice nightly and is managed by a local cultural association that secured permission from municipal authorities to operate under strict security protocols.

Organizers report that attendance has risen steadily since the venue reopened last month, with dozens of families citing the screenings as a rare opportunity for normalcy and brief respite from the war that has displaced thousands and disrupted daily life across Sudan’s capital. Security checkpoints, limited lighting and a curfew‑compliant schedule are intended to safeguard patrons, while volunteers distribute water and basic first‑aid supplies. The initiative reflects broader efforts by community groups to preserve cultural life despite the instability, offering a small but tangible sense of continuity for Khartoum’s residents.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction
content:
Experts have warned that the intense pressures associated with childhood stardom significantly increase young actors’ vulnerability to substance abuse. According to statements provided to the BBC, mental health professionals and industry observers note that the unique demands of early fame create an environment where coping mechanisms such as drug or alcohol use become more likely. This growing concern has prompted calls for greater awareness and structured support systems within the entertainment sector.

The transition from child performer to adult professional often involves navigating irregular schedules, intense public scrutiny, and early financial independence, all of which can strain developing coping skills. Specialists emphasize that the disruption of typical childhood milestones, combined with high-stakes industry expectations, may leave young actors ill-equipped to manage stress without external guidance. In response, industry advocates are urging production companies and talent agencies to implement standardized wellness protocols, ensure consistent access to counseling, and enforce stricter on-set protections to mitigate these risks.

As public discourse around performer welfare continues to evolve, stakeholders across the entertainment industry are increasingly recognizing the need for proactive safeguards. Addressing the psychological toll of early fame remains a critical step toward ensuring the long-term well-being of young talent and establishing more sustainable industry standards for future generations.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Rising data center backlash shakes up midterm races
content:
Public opposition to the rapid expansion of data centers is intensifying, prompting politicians from both parties to distance themselves from the industry. In recent weeks, community groups in several swing states have organized protests and filed zoning challenges, citing concerns over increased electricity consumption, water usage, and the visual impact of large facilities. Lawmakers in states such as Pennsylvania, Arizona and Wisconsin have introduced bills that would tighten permitting requirements, mandate higher environmental impact assessments, and require greater disclosure of corporate subsidies tied to data‑center projects.

Amid the growing backlash, candidates vying for key congressional seats are positioning themselves as advocates for stricter oversight. Several Democratic hopefuls have pledged to champion legislation that caps the size of new data‑center developments and enforces renewable‑energy sourcing, while some Republican contenders are warning that current incentives create an uneven playing field and threaten local resources. Both sides are accusing their opponents of being overly aligned with the tech sector, and the issue is shaping campaign narratives as voters increasingly view the industry’s growth as a source of environmental and community strain.
author: The Hill

title: Atlantic climate variability enables the prediction of leishmaniasis outbreaks in North Africa
content:
A new study has shown that variations in the Atlantic Ocean’s climate can forecast outbreaks of cutaneous leishmaniasis in North Africa several months before they occur. The research, led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) and conducted in partnership with the Pasteur Institutes of Tunisia, Morocco, and France, links oceanic temperature and moisture patterns to the seasonal activity of the disease’s sand‑fly vectors.

Using long‑term satellite data and epidemiological records, the team identified specific Atlantic climate indices that correlate strongly with the timing and intensity of leishmaniasis cases across Morocco, Tunisia, and Algeria. The analysis suggests that monitoring these oceanic signals could provide a reliable early‑warning system, allowing health authorities to mobilize resources, target vector control measures, and issue public advisories well before the peak transmission period.

The findings underscore the importance of integrating climate monitoring into infectious‑disease surveillance. By extending the lead time for outbreak prediction, public health agencies in the region could improve preparedness and reduce the burden of this neglected tropical disease. Further research will focus on refining the predictive model and testing its applicability in other leishmaniasis‑endemic areas.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Computer Models Find Catalysts to Replace Fossil-Fueled Ammonia Production
content:
Ammonia, the second‑most produced chemical worldwide after sulfuric acid, remains a cornerstone of global agriculture.  Its primary use is in the manufacture of nitrogen‑rich fertilizers that feed the planet’s growing population.  However, the conventional Haber‑Bosch process that produces ammonia consumes roughly 2 % of global energy and releases about 1.5 % of worldwide greenhouse‑gas emissions, underscoring the environmental cost of this essential commodity.

The industry is actively pursuing alternative production routes that could reduce both energy demand and carbon output.  Researchers and companies are evaluating renewable‑energy‑driven synthesis, electrochemical methods, and bio‑based feedstocks, all aimed at decoupling ammonia manufacture from fossil fuels.  These efforts seek to maintain the chemical’s critical role in food security while aligning with international climate targets.

As the search for greener ammonia continues, stakeholders emphasize the need for coordinated investment and policy support.  The transition to more sustainable production pathways will be pivotal in ensuring that the chemical can continue to support global food systems without exacerbating climate change.
author: Phys.org

title: US Postal Service maintains mail‑in ballot restrictions despite court ruling
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump has publicly urged the implementation of stricter limits on mail‑in voting, citing concerns over election integrity as part of a broader effort to tighten his influence over the electoral process. The call comes amid ongoing debates over voting procedures in the lead‑up to the 2024 election cycle, with the former president repeatedly asserting that absentee ballots pose a risk of fraud.

Trump’s remarks echo his previous campaigns, during which he challenged the use of mail‑in ballots and demanded increased scrutiny of absentee voting systems. He has framed the restrictions as a safeguard against alleged irregularities, while critics argue that such measures could disproportionately affect voters who rely on mail ballots for convenience or safety. The proposal has prompted responses from state officials, election boards, and civil‑rights groups, all of whom are weighing the legal and logistical implications of any new restrictions.

If enacted, the proposed limits would reshape the voting landscape, potentially altering turnout patterns and the administrative burden on election officials. The administration’s push for tighter controls remains a focal point in the national conversation about electoral security and voter access as the 2024 elections approach.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli army and settlers injure Palestinians in West Bank raids
content:
Palestinian residents of the West Bank have experienced a surge in attacks and forced displacement as Israeli settler groups expand their control over contested areas. Human rights monitors report that the expansion has been accompanied by frequent military raids, demolition orders and the demolition of homes, while the Israeli Defense Forces have largely refrained from intervening to protect the affected communities. The pattern of activity has intensified over the past several months, with dozens of villages reporting the loss of farmland and infrastructure to new settlement outposts and the relocation of residents under security pretexts.

The Israeli military has justified the operations as necessary for security and the enforcement of planning regulations, yet international observers note that the raids often target civilians and lack transparent legal procedures. The United Nations and several NGOs have called for investigations into alleged violations of international law, emphasizing that forced displacement contravenes the Fourth Geneva Convention. Israeli authorities have defended the settlements as legitimate, citing historical and religious claims, while stating that any demolition is carried out in accordance with domestic law.

The ongoing situation has heightened tensions in the region and raised concerns about the humanitarian impact on displaced Palestinians. Continued settlement growth and the perceived impunity of military actions risk further destabilizing the already fragile security environment, prompting calls from the international community for renewed diplomatic efforts to address the underlying causes of the displacement and to ensure the protection of civilian populations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Guidelines for Determining Loop Termination and Convergence
content:
a16z recently released an article titled “Knowing When to Stop: The Art of Making a Loop Converge,” which examines the critical decision point at which a startup’s iterative development cycle has reached a stable state and should be halted to move forward. The piece argues that recognizing loop convergence is essential for efficient resource allocation and avoiding the costly trap of endless experimentation.

The article lays out a framework for measuring loop performance, including quantitative thresholds and qualitative signals that indicate diminishing returns. It highlights case studies from early‑stage companies that successfully pivoted after identifying convergence, and offers practical advice on setting clear exit criteria, aligning cross‑functional teams around those metrics, and balancing the need for rapid iteration with the discipline of stopping when the loop no longer delivers incremental value.

The discussion has already sparked interest in the broader tech community, with the article appearing on Hacker News where it received four upvotes and no comments. This engagement underscores the relevance of the topic for founders and product leaders seeking to optimize their development cycles and accelerate growth.

content: A newly introduced legislative proposal seeks to modify the taxation of capital gains by indexing them for inflation and broadening the exemptions available for residential property sales. Lawmakers and policy analysts indicate that adjusting tax calculations to reflect inflationary changes could reduce the financial burden on property owners and investors,

title: USPS Tightens Mail‑In Voting Rules Amid Court Challenges
content:
The United States Postal Service announced on Friday that it will adopt new eligibility guidelines for mail‑in ballots, a move that aligns with President Donald Trump’s March executive order that limited the practice. The order, which was later invalidated by a federal court, had sought to restrict the distribution of absentee voting materials. Despite the court’s ruling, USPS said it would proceed with the guidelines as a means of complying with the executive directive.

In a 95‑page unpublished report that the agency plans to release on August 26, USPS outlined the procedures it will use to distribute mail‑in ballots for the November midterm elections. The document details the logistics of ballot delivery, eligibility verification, and the handling of absentee requests, providing a comprehensive framework for the upcoming election cycle. The report is intended to clarify how the postal service will manage ballot distribution under the new rules while maintaining compliance with federal regulations.

The announcement signals USPS’s commitment to implementing the executive order’s restrictions, even as the legal landscape surrounding absentee voting remains unsettled. The forthcoming report will offer the public and election officials a clearer view of the agency’s operational plan for the midterms, underscoring the postal service’s role in facilitating voter participation within the bounds of current policy directives.
author: The Hill

title: Local LLMs Often Seem Less Capable Due to Dataset Size and Context Limits
content:
A recent discussion on the Level1techs forum titled “Why Your Local LLM Feels Dumber Than It Is” has attracted attention from the broader tech community, including a brief thread on Hacker News. The post explains that many users experience a noticeable drop in performance when running large language models locally, compared to cloud‑hosted versions. According to the author, the primary factors are limited context windows, reduced inference speed, and the absence of continual fine‑tuning that cloud providers can apply to keep models up‑to‑date. The article also highlights that local deployments often rely on older checkpoint versions or stripped‑down architectures to fit within hardware constraints, which can further degrade output quality.

The forum thread outlines practical mitigation strategies, such as increasing the token limit, using more powerful GPUs, or integrating external knowledge bases to supplement the model’s internal memory. It also cautions that users should manage expectations: local models, while offering privacy and lower latency, cannot yet match the breadth of data and optimization that large‑scale cloud services provide. The discussion on Hacker News, which garnered 16 points and a single comment, underscores the growing interest in balancing local deployment benefits with the performance gaps that still exist. In conclusion, while local LLMs are becoming more accessible, users must weigh hardware limitations and model updates against the convenience and scale of cloud‑based solutions.
author: Hacker News

title: Browser tool adds HDR gain‑map to logos for brighter display
content:
A recent investigation revealed that a number of brand logos on LinkedIn are rendered noticeably brighter and whiter than the surrounding content when viewed on high‑dynamic‑range (HDR) displays, such as the latest MacBook Pro models. The effect is achieved by embedding a gain‑map into the JPEG files, a technique that boosts luminance only on HDR-capable screens. Unlike other social networks that strip such metadata, LinkedIn appears to preserve these gain‑maps, allowing the logos to appear more vivid to users with compatible hardware.

The discoverer collaborated with the open‑source project Claude Code to develop a lightweight, browser‑based tool that extracts and displays the enhanced logos without requiring registration. The utility can be accessed via a public URL and is designed to help designers and marketers verify how their brand imagery will appear on HDR devices. The tool has attracted modest attention on Hacker News, where it received 18 up‑votes and 15 comments, indicating interest from the developer community.

While the practice of embedding gain‑maps is not widespread, its use on LinkedIn highlights a niche area of digital asset optimization that may become more relevant as HDR displays become standard. The availability of a free, no‑registration utility offers a practical solution for stakeholders who wish to ensure consistent brand presentation across diverse viewing environments.

title: DOJ investigates Andreessen Horowitz over startup board seat practices
content:
The U.S. Department of Justice announced a formal investigation into the practice of allocating board seats to venture‑capital‑backed startups, a development highlighted in the most recent episode of the “Equity” podcast. The probe, launched earlier this month, focuses on whether the arrangement of board appointments—often tied to financing rounds—violates antitrust laws by potentially restricting competition, influencing market entry, or creating undue influence over emerging companies.

Regulators are reviewing a sample of recent financing deals in which investors secured board positions as a condition of capital infusion, examining the terms of those agreements and any accompanying non‑compete or exclusivity clauses. Industry observers note that the inquiry could reshape standard venture‑capital practices, prompting firms to reassess governance structures and disclosure requirements. The DOJ has not indicated any immediate enforcement actions, but the investigation underscores heightened scrutiny of corporate governance arrangements within the tech startup ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Iran allows select Iraqi oil tankers to transit Hormuz
content:
Baghdad – Iraqi President Nizar Amidi declared that Iraq’s territory will not be employed as a launchpad for attacks against any other state, emphasizing the nation’s commitment to uphold its sovereignty and regional stability. The statement was made during a press briefing in the capital, where Amidi responded to growing concerns from neighboring countries about the possible use of Iraqi soil by non‑state actors to conduct cross‑border operations.

Amidi’s remarks come amid heightened diplomatic pressure following a series of incidents in which militias based in Iraq were alleged to have fired rockets toward neighboring territories. The Iraqi government has repeatedly called for the disarmament of armed groups operating within its borders and has pledged to strengthen border controls and intelligence cooperation with regional partners. In the same briefing, officials outlined ongoing efforts to curtail the flow of weapons and to enforce existing security agreements, underscoring that any violation would be treated as a breach of Iraq’s international obligations.

The president’s unequivocal stance reinforces Baghdad’s policy of non‑intervention and signals to the international community that Iraq intends to prevent its territory from being exploited for hostile actions. By reaffirming these principles, the Iraqi leadership aims to mitigate external tensions and maintain a neutral posture in an increasingly volatile Middle‑East environment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Sudan's Kordofan Sees Over 200,000 Displaced Amid Fighting
content:
Intensified fighting in Sudan’s western Kordofan region has forced at least 200,000 residents to flee their homes since late last year.  The clashes, which have escalated between government forces and armed opposition groups, have disrupted local livelihoods and destroyed infrastructure, prompting mass displacement into nearby towns and camps.

Humanitarian agencies report that the displaced population faces acute shortages of food, clean water and medical supplies.  Over 70 aid organizations have mobilized emergency relief efforts, but access remains limited due to ongoing hostilities and damaged transportation routes.  The United Nations has called for an immediate ceasefire and safe corridors for civilians, while the Sudanese government has pledged to provide shelter and assistance to those displaced.

The displacement crisis underscores the urgent need for a durable political solution to the conflict.  International observers warn that without a negotiated settlement, the humanitarian situation in Kordofan could deteriorate further, risking widespread famine and disease outbreaks.  The international community continues to monitor the situation closely, urging all parties to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel opens construction bids for new housing units in occupied West Bank
content:
Israel’s Ministry of Housing has issued a public tender to build a new batch of housing units in the occupied West Bank, despite the projects being classified as illegal under Israeli regulations because they lack the required building permits. The bid, announced on Monday, invites contractors to submit proposals for the construction of multiple residential units in areas adjacent to existing Israeli settlements.

The tender follows a pattern of settlement expansion that has drawn criticism from the Palestinian Authority and several international bodies, which consider such construction a breach of international law. Israeli officials contend that the housing addresses demographic needs of Israeli citizens in the region. The contracts are expected to be awarded in the coming weeks, and the development is set to proceed pending the completion of the bidding process, maintaining the contentious status of settlement activity in the West Bank.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Togo claims evidence against detained French filmmakers
content:
Togo’s government announced on Saturday that it possessed “serious and corroborative evidence” against two French documentary filmmakers who were arrested last month together with their Togolese fixer. The authorities say the evidence supports charges that the men made false declarations, a claim the trio denies. The case has drawn attention from both the French media community and human‑rights observers, who have expressed concern over the legal process and the filmmakers’ right to a fair trial.

The arrest followed a series of investigations into the production of a documentary that the Togolese authorities allege contained fabricated statements about government officials. The filmmakers, whose identities have not yet been disclosed, were detained in a high‑security facility pending further inquiry. Their fixer, a local journalist, was also charged with complicity in the alleged false statements. Togo’s Ministry of Justice has called for an expedited judicial review, while the French Embassy has urged that the defendants be treated in accordance with international legal standards.

As the case moves forward, both sides remain steadfast. The filmmakers maintain that their work was conducted with journalistic integrity and that the accusations are politically motivated. Meanwhile, the Togolese government insists that the evidence is conclusive and that the legal proceedings will proceed without delay. The outcome will likely influence future collaborations between Togolese authorities and foreign media practitioners.
author: France 24

title: Swedish police identify 17‑year‑old victim in school sword attack
content:
The principal of Brinell School confirmed that the 18‑year‑old suspect identified by police in connection with Friday’s deadly sword attack was enrolled at the institution. The assault, which took place at a nearby community center on Friday afternoon, resulted in three fatalities and several injuries before the assailant was subdued by security personnel. Authorities have placed the suspect in custody and are conducting a forensic examination of the weapon and the crime scene.

Law enforcement officials said the investigation is ongoing and that they are reviewing surveillance footage and interviewing witnesses to establish a motive. The school has activated its crisis‑response protocol, offering counseling services to students and staff while cooperating fully with investigators. No further threats have been reported, and officials emphasized that public safety measures remain in effect as the case proceeds through the legal system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel and Turkey clash over Syria, challenging regional consensus
content:
Israel’s recent military operations in Syria have intensified tensions not only with Turkey but also with a broad coalition of regional and international actors. In the past month, the Israeli Defense Forces conducted a series of airstrikes targeting Iranian-backed militia positions near the Golan Heights, citing the need to prevent the transfer of advanced weaponry to hostile groups. The strikes, which reportedly hit multiple sites in the eastern Homs and Idlib provinces, were met with condemnation from Ankara, which accused Israel of violating Syrian sovereignty and escalating the conflict.

Turkey’s reaction has been swift and forceful. Ankara has deployed additional naval and air assets to the eastern Mediterranean, and its foreign ministry has called for an urgent UN Security Council meeting to address the “unilateral” Israeli actions. Meanwhile, the United Nations and several Arab states have reiterated calls for a cessation of hostilities and the protection of civilian populations in Syria. The broader international community, including the United States and European Union, has urged restraint, noting that Israel’s operations risk destabilizing an already fragile ceasefire framework established by the Geneva peace talks.

The convergence of these diplomatic pressures underscores a growing consensus that Israel’s conduct in Syria deviates from accepted norms. While Israel maintains that its strikes are defensive measures against Iranian influence, the combined response from Turkey, the UN, and regional partners signals a unified stance against unilateral military actions that threaten to widen the Syrian conflict. As diplomatic channels remain strained, the situation remains volatile, with potential implications for regional stability and international law.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canada to impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods from September 8
content:
The United States announced a 50 percent tariff on nearly $20 billion of Canadian imports, targeting sectors that include aluminum, steel, and a range of consumer goods. Hours after the measure was disclosed, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau addressed the nation, emphasizing that the tariffs constitute a “significant escalation” in the ongoing trade dispute and reaffirming his government’s commitment to defending Canadian interests.

Trudeau outlined a multi‑track response that will involve consultations with American officials, a formal request for a review through the World Trade Organization, and the exploration of counter‑measures consistent with international trade rules. He noted that the tariffs could raise costs for Canadian exporters and downstream businesses, potentially affecting employment in affected industries. The prime minister concluded by urging both governments to return to dialogue to resolve the issue and restore a stable trading relationship.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US official accuses Israel of not notifying before Syrian strike
content:
U.S. official Tom Barrack publicly accused Israel of failing to provide the United States with sufficient advance notice regarding a recent security development, alleging that the lack of warning jeopardized American interests. Barrack’s remarks, made during a briefing in Washington, referenced a specific incident in which Israeli forces conducted a rapid operation that resulted in collateral damage affecting U.S. personnel stationed in the region. He asserted that prior notification would have allowed American authorities to take precautionary measures and mitigate potential risks.

The Israeli government rejected Barrack’s claim, stating that no formal warning was required under existing bilateral protocols and that the operation was conducted in accordance with international law. A spokesperson for the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized that Israel routinely shares relevant intelligence with its allies, and that any perceived lapse was a misunderstanding rather than a deliberate omission. Both sides affirmed their commitment to continued coordination, while diplomatic channels remain open to address any future communication concerns.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Curiosity Rover Finds Massive Polygon Field on Mars
content:
Mars boasts some of the most striking and diverse landscapes in the solar system, a fact that has captivated scientists and the public alike. The planet’s surface displays towering volcanoes, vast canyon systems, and expansive dune fields that remain largely unchanged over billions of years.

This remarkable preservation is largely due to the absence of dynamic resurfacing mechanisms found on Earth. Mars lacks active plate tectonics, sustained volcanic activity, and flowing liquid water, all of which on Earth continually reshape the planet’s crust. Consequently, ancient geological features on Mars have endured, offering a pristine record of the planet’s early history and climatic evolution.

The static nature of Mars’ surface provides a unique laboratory for studying planetary geology. By examining these enduring formations, researchers can gain insights into the processes that once shaped the planet, helping to refine models of planetary evolution across the solar system.
author: Phys.org

title: Seven dead, including two police officers, in UK wrong‑side collision
content:
A serious traffic collision occurred on Tuesday evening on the A12 near Dagenham, involving three vehicles and resulting in two people being taken to hospital with serious injuries. The crash follows a series of similar incidents in Ireland, where police have identified a social media trend that encourages drivers to reverse direction on motorways. In the Irish cases, the trend, popularized on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, led to several fatal and non‑fatal accidents before authorities issued a public warning.

Investigators in England are examining the circumstances of the Dagenham collision, noting that preliminary evidence suggests a driver may have been influenced by the same online challenge. Irish police, after a month of increased crashes, released a statement urging motorists to avoid any form of “reverse driving” and to report any suspicious behaviour. The trend, which gained traction in late 2023, has prompted both the UK and Irish transport departments to collaborate on a cross‑border safety campaign.

Both jurisdictions are reinforcing road safety messages through media outlets and social platforms. Officials stress that any deviation from standard driving directions remains illegal and dangerous, and they are urging the public to remain vigilant and report any attempts to spread the trend.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US deportations to Liberia spark uncertainty and political backlash
content:
Liberian officials announced on Tuesday a change to the schedule of a scheduled international flight that was set to depart on Thursday. The government stated that the adjustment was necessary to accommodate operational requirements and to ensure the safety of passengers and crew. The announcement came two days before the flight, leaving little time for airlines and passengers to adjust.

Members of the opposition and several lawmakers have criticized the decision, saying they were not consulted before the announcement. They argue that the lack of coordination with the aviation ministry and the airlines could lead to confusion and logistical challenges. The government has not yet released details on how the change will affect ticket holders or the airline’s operations.

The situation remains under review as the airline and the civil aviation authority work to communicate the new schedule to passengers. Both sides have indicated that they will seek to minimize disruption while maintaining compliance with international aviation standards.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump seeks to block BBC subpoena of Ivanka and Trump Jr.
content:
The United States president’s legal team has dismissed recent subpoenas issued by congressional investigators as “cynical,” arguing that the requests are politically motivated and lack substantive evidence. The subpoenas, which seek documents and testimony related to the president’s administration, have been met with a defensive stance that the inquiries are an attempt to undermine the president’s authority rather than a legitimate effort to uncover wrongdoing.

The BBC, however, has cautioned that the subpoenas could serve an important role in clarifying the matter. In a statement, the broadcaster noted that the documents and testimony requested could provide transparency and help the public understand the facts surrounding the case. The BBC emphasized that while the subpoenas may be contentious, they also present an opportunity for the investigation to be conducted openly and for any potential misconduct to be examined under the scrutiny of the media and the public.
author: Al Jazeera
